Scope of Work by Construction Phase:1. Pre-Construction Planning & Permitting•	Perform Manual J load calculation for heating/cooling loads.•	Prepare Manual D duct design for air distribution.•	Select HVAC equipment per Manual S sizing standards.•	Submit equipment specifications, cut sheets, and duct layout with permit package to City of Dallas.•	Coordinate with builder/general contractor for mechanical chase, soffit, and utility penetration planning.2. Rough-In Stage (Prior to Insulation & Drywall)•	Install all supply and return ductwork (R-8 insulated flexible duct for unconditioned spaces, per Dallas/IECC).•	Install sheet metal trunk lines, plenums, and boots per Manual D layout.•	Install refrigerant line sets between indoor air handler/coil and outdoor condensing unit.•	Run condensate drain lines to approved termination points (with primary & secondary drains per IMC §307).•	Install bathroom exhaust fans, kitchen vent ductwork, and dryer vent duct with exterior termination.•	Frame and set HVAC platform (attic or mechanical closet as per plans).•	Install combustion air ducts (if gas furnace is used).•	Install venting for furnaces and water heaters (Category IV PVC or B-vent, as applicable).•	Install gas piping to furnace (if applicable) with sediment traps, shutoff valve, and pressure test per IFGC.•	Provide fresh air intake/mechanical ventilation system in compliance with Dallas Energy Code.•	Seal all ductwork connections with mastic or UL-listed tape (per IECC).3. Equipment Installation•	Install air handler/furnace unit in attic or mechanical closet.•	Install outdoor condensing unit on approved pad or platform, meeting Dallas setback and clearance requirements.•	Connect refrigerant lines, pressure test, and evacuate system prior to charging.•	Install line-set insulation with UV protection where exposed.•	Connect electrical whips, disconnects, breakers, and thermostat wiring per NEC.•	Connect gas piping (if applicable), perform pressure test, and verify for leaks.•	Set and level drain pans with float switches and secondary drains.•	Install supply registers, return grilles, exhaust grilles in planned locations.________________________________________4. Trim-Out & Final Connections•	Install programmable thermostat(s) per IECC requirements.•	Install final supply/return registers and grilles.•	Install bath exhaust fan trim kits and kitchen vent termination hood.•	Seal penetrations at ceiling/walls for air barrier integrity.•	Charge refrigerant system per manufacturer specs and Dallas code requirements.•	Balance air distribution system to provide correct airflow to each room.•	Verify combustion air and venting operation (if gas furnace).•	Test condensate drains for proper slope and drainage.________________________________________5. Testing, Commissioning & Final Inspection•	Perform duct leakage testing per IECC (? 4 CFM/100 sq. ft. at 25 Pa).•	Perform airflow balancing for proper CFM per room.•	Test gas piping and connections for leaks.•	Verify thermostat and system operational controls.•	Provide manufacturer startup sheets, equipment model/serials, and balancing report to homeowner and inspector.•	Schedule City of Dallas final inspection for mechanical systems.________________________________________Owner-Supplied vs. Contractor-Supplied•	Contractor will provide and install all HVAC equipment, ductwork, registers, grills, refrigerant piping, gas piping, and associated materials unless otherwise noted.•	Builder/homeowner to coordinate mechanical chase framing and access to electrical service.Exclusions•	Removal of asbestos or hazardous materials.•	Structural modifications not shown in HVAC plans.•	Utility company fees for gas or electrical service upgrades
